messages:
Eli: Ran a full perf sweep on canary for mixed FP8/INT8 kernels with continuous-batcher + KV cache prefilling. Saw a consistent 11-14% tail latency regression for seq_len 512-1024 on A100s compared to master

Maya: ugh. Is that with padding-aware kernel selection enabled?

Eli: yes. config used:
```
batcher: continuous
padding_policy: trim-prefix
kernel_selector: dynamic
quant_profile: fp8-int8-hybrid
kvcache_mode: slab-split
```

Thomas: Can you paste the perf numbers? p50/p95/p99.

Eli: p50: 18ms -> 19ms (+5%)
p95: 42ms -> 48ms (+14%)
p99: 120ms -> 138ms (+15%)

Eli: heap profile shows increased memcpy and small-kernel-launch overhead; traces link: https://perf.redwood/trace/abc123

Miguel: looks like more kernel launches when batches have mixed padding shapes, and fp8 kernels don't support packed-rows -> causing fallback to int8 kernel for some heads.

Maya: is calibration different? maybe per-tensor vs per-channel causing shape mismatch?

Eli: calibration unchanged. But quantizer emits a different packing decision when sequence shapes vary; basically we get more "fragmented slabs" in KV cache which forces per-request copy into contiguous buffer.

Thomas: so padding waste + copy overhead + kernel shape mismatch. Can we force "shape-coalescing" in batcher? i.e., group by shape before dispatch.

Eli: I ran a quick patch that groups by (seq_len, quant_shape) in the continuous batcher. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3421

Eli: results after grouping:
p50: 18ms -> 18ms (no change)
p95: 42ms -> 44ms (+4.7%)
p99: 120ms -> 126ms (+5%)
So much better.

Miguel: any accuracy/regression from grouping? need to check QA evals.

Maya: also curious about KV cache slab-split logic. Can we change split threshold to avoid tiny slabs?

Eli: yes, tuning threshold from 64->128 reduces tiny slab count by ~70% in profile.

Thomas: propose: merge PR with grouping + adjust slab threshold + add metric for kernel-fallback-rate. Add rollout canary 10% and monitor p99 & fallback-rate.

Eli: added canary config in deploy: `canary: {percent:10, metric: p99_latency, alert: fallback_rate>0.5%}`

Ci-bot: deploy started for runtime-canary/3421 at 1839999001 :rocket:

Maya: monitoring dashboard link: https://dash.redwood/canary/3421

Thomas: let's also add telemetry event when quantizer chooses fallback path (tag kernel_variant=fallback). Need minimal perf impact to emit.

Eli: agree. I'll send a small telemetry PR.

Miguel: :thumbsup: If canary looks good, let's backfill into dedicated/hosted configs.

Eli: OK will run extended eval overnight and report tomorrow. :coffee:

Ci-bot: canary finished: success at 1839999050. Logs: https://ci.redwood/jobs/7654

Maya: preliminary: fallback_rate dropped from 1.8% -> 0.4%, p99 improved ~9% vs previous canary. Good.

Thomas: thanks team. followups: add unit test for slab-split logic, perf test for grouping. I'll file issues.

Maya: filing: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/523

Eli: done. Will sync in tomorrow standup.
